claim: China's 240-hour visa-free transit covers nationals of 55 countries and requires valid travel documents and onward tickets with confirmed seats/dates, applying at 65 ports in 24 provinces/regions/municipalities.
quote: nationals of 55 countries including Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States ... valid international travel documents and onward tickets with confirmed seats and departure dates ... designated 65 open exit-entry ports in 24 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities

claim: The transit stay was extended from 72/144 hours to 240 hours (10 days), with Shanghai and Zhejiang among the eligible provincial regions.
quote: from the previous 72 hours and 144 hours to 240 hours (10 days) ... 60 open ports in 24 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities)

claim: Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao airports and Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport are explicitly listed as eligible entry ports for the visa-free transit policy.
quote: Shanghai's Pudong and Hongqiao airports, Shanghai Port (Passenger) ... Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport

claim: Foreign tourists in 2026 can bind an international Visa or Mastercard directly to Alipay and WeChat Pay using only a passport and home-country phone number, no Chinese bank account required.
quote: Foreigners can absolutely use Alipay in China in 2026 without needing a Chinese bank account or Chinese phone number - you just need a valid passport, an international Visa or Mastercard, and a working phone number from your home country.

claim: WeChat Pay supports direct foreign card binding for Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover and Maestro, requiring a passport whose name matches the card.
quote: WeChat Pay accepts Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover, and Maestro ... Valid passport — required for identity verification. Name on card must match name on passport exactly.

claim: Foreign tourists link their Visa/Mastercard to Alipay's International Version; single transactions under 200 RMB are free, with a 3% service fee above that.
quote: Link your Visa/Mastercard ... For most platforms, single transactions under 200 RMB (~$28) are FREE. For transactions over 200 RMB, a 3% service fee is usually applied.
